findings.metric: Online production trip creation uses Firestore-authoritative numbering
findings.details: When online, the TripNumberGenerator invokes doc/runTransaction inside systemCounters/tripNumber_{projectId} which guarantees sequential, centralized numbering.

findings.metric: In-memory fallback cannot create duplicate or conflicting trip numbers
findings.details: Unsafe path identified: Offline or unauthenticated clients fall back to an in-memory counter starting at 1. If another client has created online/offline trips with index 1, syncing the offline record will write duplicate tripNumber attributes inside Firestore because there is no unique constraint on tripNumber attributes.

findings.metric: Offline trip creation behavior is explicitly defined
findings.details: Fallback code paths are defined inside TripNumberGenerator.getNextTripNumber, reverting to in-memory counter tracking (Record<string, number>) on catch block or if auth context is missing.

findings.metric: Synchronization after offline operation cannot duplicate tripNumber
findings.details: Since trips are saved to subcollections /projects/{projectId}/trips/{tripId} using a random UUID as the document ID, Firestore rules permit direct client-side creation. No unique index, constraint, or server-side sync check blocks the persistence of duplicate tripNumber attributes, leading to duplicate identifiers.

findings.metric: Failed transactions cannot consume or reuse an unsafe number
findings.details: Firestore transactions roll back completely on failure, meaning the counter nextNumber is not mutated on the server if transaction retries exhaust or fail. Consumed sequences are continuous.

findings.metric: Concurrent users cannot generate the same trip number
findings.details: For active online concurrent requests, Firestore server-side transactions serialize execution, preventing race conditions or duplicate sequence numbers between multiple online dispatchers.

findings.metric: Existing historical trip numbers remain immutable
findings.details: Firestore security rules enforce that delete actions on trips are blocked (allow delete: if false), and updates to tripNumber are blocked once defined.

findings.metric: Client cannot supply or override tripNumber
findings.details: Vulnerability identified: Firestore security rules allow clients to write any payload on trip creation. A malicious client can bypass TripNumberGenerator completely and specify an arbitrary or pre-existing tripNumber value directly in the document create request.

findings.metric: Project prefix always matches the projectNumber
findings.details: Prefix is formatted dynamically as Q-PRJ-{projectNumber} utilizing project metadata fetched either via arguments or real-time lookup.
Counter state is isolated on document paths systemCounters/tripNumber_{projectId} and partitioned in memory via projectId keys, ensuring strict isolation.

unsafe_paths.description: Falling back to in-memory counters (e.g. 1) generates local duplicates of sequence numbers already consumed by online users. Reconnection uploads duplicate tripNumbers.
unsafe_paths.minimum_fix: Enforce trip creation strictly via backend APIs where sequential allocation is performed server-side on Express server during persistence, and enforce read-only status on tripNumber at the client rules level.

unsafe_paths.description: Rules do not validate that incoming().tripNumber corresponds to an authorized, calculated sequential index, allowing clients to inject arbitrary numbers.
unsafe_paths.minimum_fix: Inhibit client-side create permissions on /projects/{projectId}/trips and delegate creation exclusively to secure API routes under Server SDK credentials.
